input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: research track draw: track 23 (marine), next free milestone 9 marine-detect
errors: First evaluation counted zero floating obstacles: MaSTr1325 leaves an unknown margin round each object, so a 1-px ring saw only ignored pixels; fixed with a 3-px ring (stable 204 to 189 for rings 3 to 8) and reran all seeds (about 20 minutes lost).
Backgrounded a long training job with '&' once instead of run_in_background; killed and relaunched it properly.

doc_friction.issue: Says check 'python3 -c import torch' first; the default /usr/local/bin/python3 lacks torch and has a broken PIL under -I, while /usr/bin/python3 (3.13, where pip installs) got torch from the CPU index in about a minute. Naming /usr/bin/python3 as the interpreter to check would have saved several calls.
Downloaded-data rule (run Python with -I) breaks here: -I makes /usr/bin/python3 PIL imports fail via the distutils-precedence.pth hack; running from the repo cwd with paths as arguments works.
Research CI runs the homepage build and programme check but no project tests, so the PR's 10 tests ran only locally.

deviations.why: Milestone 9 says 'reproduce a published segmentation baseline'; WaSR needs the IMU channel and a ResNet-101 that a 4-core CPU cannot train in a session, and MODS evaluation was not attempted.
deviations.did: Trained the published LR-ASPP MobileNetV3 architecture instead and labelled it a baseline, not a reproduction; MODS and WaSR listed as next steps.
deviations.result: A complete 9a step with 3 seeds per model landed; comparison with published numbers still open.

notes: Data: MaSTr1325 512x384 images+masks from data.vicos.si (CC BY 4.0), sha256 recorded in data.py. Local checks: pytest 10 passed (/usr/bin/python3), research/_homepage/build.py ok, research_live_links --write, check_md_links ok, programme_check ok, cite_check all 7 ids ok, post frontmatter/links/tag-balance ok. Training: 9 runs, 12-13 min per LR-ASPP run on 4 cores; total about 2 h. No agent doc in docs/reports: the README Next steps and LOG carry what the next run needs.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: an ML engineer setting up data, split, metrics, 9 CPU trainings and the write-up: about three days

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
